title: Comprehensive Ophthalmic Laser Procedures
summary: An exhaustive clinical guide to laser applications in the retina, glaucoma management, and lens surgery. This manual details specific indications, precise laser settings, procedural methodologies, and critical complication profiles for world-class ophthalmic care.

sections.title: PRP Red Flags & Complications
content: Permanent loss of peripheral field (driving implications)
Worsened acuity (macular decompensation or inadvertent macular laser)

sections.title: Macular Laser (Focal or Grid)
content: Consent: Explain reduction of sight loss, need for retreatment, pain, scotomas, worsened acuity, retinal/choroidal detachment.
Prep: Topical anaesthetic + fundus CL (e.g. area centralis) with coupling agent.
Settings: 532nm/green; 50-200 micron spot; 0.08–0.1s; very gentle blanching burn. Smaller/shorter for central burns.
Focal Technique: Burns to microaneurysms 500-3000 microns from foveal centre (min 300 if outside FAZ).
Grid Technique: Burns ≥1 burn-width apart around fovea; min 500 microns from foveal centre and disc margin.

branches: Indications: Retinal break with RD risk (usually U-tears) without excessive SRF
Slit-lamp: For equatorial and post-equatorial lesions
Indirect: For anterior lesions (with indentation) or cryotherapy

sections.title: Nd-YAG Peripheral Iridotomy (PI)
content: Indications: Angle closure with pupil block (Acute/Subacute/Chronic/1°/2°) & Prophylaxis for occludable angles.
Consent: Explain purpose, bilateral treatment, failure risk, bleeding, inflammation, corneal burns, monocular diplopia.
Pre-Medication: Pilocarpine 2% (iris tension) + Apraclonidine 1% (IOP spike/bleeding prevention) + Anaesthetic.
Laser Setup: 2-3 pulse bursts of 3–6mJ (higher for thick/pigmented irides); Angle the beam (not perpendicular).
Site Selection: Superior (under lid), peripheral, ideally in iris crypt.
Execution: Focus and fire; success shown by forward gush of pigment-loaded aqueous (usually 2–4 shots).
Post-op: Topical steroid (dexamethasone 0.1% 6x/d for 1wk); IOP check at 30-60min; Review within 10d.

sections.title: Nd-YAG PI Complications
content: Glare and optical aberrations (avoid interpalpebral area/tear meniscus)

sections.title: Argon Laser Peripheral Iridoplasty (ALPI)
content: Method: Ring of burns to peripheral iris stroma (Abraham/Goldmann lens).
Applications: 20–50 burns over 360° (≥2 spot sizes apart).
Complications: Inflammation (mild), IOP spike, corneal burns.

rows: Intractable IOP (rubeotic/synechial); unwell patients; temporizing pre-trab.
Refractory IOP; easier in pseudophakic eyes; can combine with Phaco.
Contact probe 0.5–2mm from limbus; 5–10 shots per quadrant.
Limbal or pars plana; laser process until shrinkage/whitening.
Avoid 3/9 o’clock and superior quadrant; avoid audible 'pops'.
Fill AC with viscoelastic; avoid treating 'valleys'; avoid 'pops'.
Antibiotics, Steroids, continue glaucoma meds; oral acetazolamide stat.

sections.title: Nd-YAG Posterior Capsulotomy
content: Caution: Assess for uveitis, glaucoma, macular oedema, retinal degeneration (high-risk).
Prep: Mydriatics (Tropicamide 1% ± Phenylephrine 2.5%); Capsulotomy lens + coupling agent.
Settings: 1–1.5mJ (higher for thicker PCO); Angle the beam.
Technique 1 (Full Ring): Posterior capsulorhexis (detached capsule free-floating).
Technique 2 (Partial Ring): Inferior hinge (capsule drops but stays attached).
Technique 3 (Cross): Peripheral start in each axis.
Post-op: Topical steroid 4x/d 2wk; Review 4–6 weeks for visual axis clarity and inflammation check.

rows: Cataract: Clear corneal incisions, LRIs, capsulorhexis, lens fragmentation. Refractive: LASIK flaps, ICRS channels, keratoplasty cuts.
Ablative reshaping of the cornea for PRK, LASIK, and LASEK.
